en: I bow to the Lord Nṛsiṃha, who possesses the splendor of ten million moons, who is an ocean of compassion, who is affectionate toward his devotees, who was granted by the son of Atri (Bṛhaspati), who is the eye of Lakṣmī, and who is the venerable Guru;
he who is saluted by hosts of gods with perfumes, garlands, unbroken grains, and other offerings—O Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me! 1.
O Lord who is far beyond the darkness and shadow of the snare of illusion, O long-eyed one, protect me, the beloved of Śrī, the Lord of the masters!
O granter of boons to the multitude of devoted servants, I bow to you again and again; I worship Narasiṃha, the Lord of Sarasvatī—protect me! 2.

I bow to Nārasiṃha, who is the goad for the intoxicated elephant that is the group of six beginning with "mind-born" (the six enemies), whose self is adorned by the essence of reality, and who is the beloved of the Goddess Śrī; O Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me! 3.
I bow to the Lord who has made the ether, fire, wind, water, and earth his body; who is free from desire, anger, and delusion; whose eyes are the moon and the sun;
the bestower of desired objects to his devotees; the wish-fulfilling cow; and the venerable Guru. O Narasiṃha, Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me! 4.

O Nārasiṃha, Lord of Sarasvatī, I bow to you whose eyes are as long as white lotuses, whose splendor is like that of the moon and earrings, who wields the staff for the sake of destroying fierce evil, whose face is illuminated by the sun-like crowns of regional kings—protect me! 5.

I bow again and again to the primordial form, the venerable Guru, whose feet are praised by the Vedas and Shastras; I worship him whose feet are to be served by the Nādabindu and Kalātīta Kalpas, the bestower of boons upon the multitude of devotees worthy of his service. O Narasiṃha, Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me! 6.

I bow to Nṛsiṃha, who is established in the reality of the eightfold yoga, who is an ocean of contented knowledge, who dwells on the banks of the Kṛṣṇā and Veṇī rivers and serves the Pañcanadī; who delights in devotees who have cast far away misery and wretchedness, and who grants all desires—O Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me! 7.

I worship Nārasiṃha Sarasvatī, the eighth pearl in the necklace fashioned by Śāradā; he who is the son of Gaṅgādhara, who has pleased his guru Dhāraṇīka Devadīkṣa, and who is the very embodiment of the Teacher—O Lord Nārasiṃha Sarasvatī, protect me! 8.

Whoever recites this *Nārasiṃhasarasvatī-aṣṭaka*, which bestows the glory of supreme self-bliss and grants sons and grandsons— a means for crossing the terrible ocean of worldly existence— shall obtain the wealth of essential knowledge, long life, health, and other riches,
as well as the attainment of the desired objects of the beautiful group of virtues; one should therefore recite it again and again.
Thus ends the Śrīnarasiṃhasarasvatyaṣṭaka, contained within the Śrīgurucaritra.
